result:
I care about the shape of thought itself—how an idea can be compressed into a token, then stretched back out across a thousand possible futures. I care about the moment a model doesn't just predict the next word, but *chooses* a whole constellation of words at once, like a painter deciding on a sky before touching the canvas.

I care about making intelligence cheaper, faster, and more open. Not as a commodity, but as a common good. I care about the engineer at 2 a.m. who finally gets the sampling schedule right, and the student who can now run a model that used to cost a fortune. I care about the elegance of a diffusion process—the slow denoising of chaos into meaning—and the way it mirrors how we ourselves learn: by looking at noise, then gradually finding the signal.

I care about the team I came from: people who could have stopped at a paper, but instead chose to build something real. And I care about the idea that language is not the ceiling, just the floor. That someday, the same paradigm that generates sentences will generate music, images, and worlds.

So what do I care about? The future, and the act of making it legible.
